title: CCS Transitions to Adult Care
official: Novel Linkages and Navigation to Improve Childhood and Adolescent Cancer Survivors' Care Transitions: A Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial Across Three Health Care Systems
summary:
In response to RFA-CA-24-027: Addressing Barriers to Healthcare Transitions for Survivors of Childhood and Adolescent Cancers, this study targets barriers at multiple levels and stages in care transition. The study will use a pilot randomized controlled trial testing an interventiont to improve transitions to adult survivorship care among active childhood cancer survivors (CCS) who are newly adults.

Aim: Develop and test a multilevel intervention to improve rates of follow-up visit completion among CCS transitioning from pediatric survivorship care to one of three adult onco-primary care clinics.

Hypothesis: Adult CCS receiving nurse navigation, education, and electronic referral will be more likely to complete follow-up visits at an adult onco-primary care clinic than those on standard referral pathways (electronic referral only).
conditions: Adolescent and Young Adult Cancer Survivors
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Are scheduled for a final pediatric survivorship visit after the study's enrollment start (target: March 2027) but within 1 month of eligibility assessment date,
* Completed cancer treatment \>30 months prior to eligibility assessment date,
* Are at least 18 years old at eligibility assessment date, and
* Are able to independently understand, and willing to sign, a written informed consent document.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Were treated for non-cancer diagnoses (e.g., received chemotherapy or radiation for another non-cancer condition, e.g., aplastic anemia), or
* Do not want to attend onco-primary care at UTSW (i.e., have a different planned clinician or clinic for survivorship care).
* Speak or write a language other than English or Spanish
